hypotheses.justification: The statement is still true for u = ∅. There polytopeSoftPartition ∅ delta theta is an empty sum, so it equals 0. Then polytopeSoftSupport ∅ delta theta = delta * Real.log 0 = 0, using Real.log 0 = 0. So polytopeRoundedSupport ∅ delta rho is the constant function rho. Its first and second derivatives are 0. smoothSupportCurve h theta = h theta • n + deriv h theta • (n*I), where n = circleMap 0 1 theta. This reduces to rho • n, and its derivative is rho • (n*I). That is nonzero because rho > 0 and ‖n‖ = 1. Equivalently, smoothSupportCurvatureRadius = rho + 0 > 0, so smoothSupportCurve_regular applies, and it needs only ContDiff ℝ ∞ h and positivity of the radius. The proof changes only by a case split. If u.Nonempty, use the existing proof. Otherwise use Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty to get u = ∅, then simp [polytopeRoundedSupport, polytopeSoftSupport, polytopeSoftPartition] shows the support function is const rho. Then contDiff_const gives smoothness, and deriv_const (twice) gives the radius rho > 0. hu is used only through contDiff_polytopeRoundedSupport and polytopeRoundedSupport_add_deriv_deriv_pos, and both need it only to keep Real.log away from 0. The statement itself does not mention hu beyond u. hdelta and hrho are not claimed removable.
